response.sql: WITH scans_in_range AS (SELECT s.zoneref, s.gbsize, s.spanmin, st.healtheval FROM scans s JOIN sites st ON s.zoneref = st.zoneregistry WHERE s.chronotag >= '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274' AND s.chronotag <= '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797'), group_stats AS (SELECT zoneref, healtheval, AVG(CASE WHEN gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL AND spanmin > 0 THEN 1.0 * gbsize / spanmin END) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS scan_count FROM scans_in_range GROUP BY zoneref, healtheval), mean_value AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM group_stats WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL), filtered_groups AS (SELECT gs.zoneref, gs.healtheval, gs.avg_ratio, gs.scan_count, gs.avg_ratio - mv.overall_mean AS excess_amount FROM group_stats gs CROSS JOIN mean_value mv WHERE mv.overall_mean IS NOT NULL AND gs.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL AND gs.avg_ratio > mv.overall_mean) SELECT zoneref, healtheval, avg_ratio, scan_count, excess_amount FROM filtered_groups ORDER BY excess_amount DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: chronotag is stored in a text or timestamp format compatible with direct comparison to ISO datetime strings. The schema declares chronotag as text(6) (too short for a full datetime), but the documentation suggests it may be a TIMESTAMP or Excel serial number. The query assumes direct text comparison with the provided ISO strings will work.
Scans with spanmin ≤ 0 are excluded from the average ratio calculation to prevent division by zero, but are still counted in scan_count for each group.
